requirement:
The `habeas-refactor` skill MUST direct agents to make the move with their own
edits, keeping it separate from any change to the moved code or text; to run
`habeas refactor --dry-run` under {cite}`requirements.refactor.dry_run` with a
mapping for every moved file, node, and definition name under
{cite}`requirements.refactor.mappings`; to review its report, including
records it would leave unchanged and the rationale spans it lists under
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.untouched`; to run it without

are stale; and to commit the move and evidence update before changing
behavior, then reassess stale records with `habeas author` under the
habeas-evidence skill.
rationale:
The subject is about the text of the bundled `habeas-refactor` skill. The only `{test}` item is `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_refactor_skill_moves_first_then_updates_evidence_with_habeas_refactor]`. It calls `assert_in_order`, which runs `assert_text_in_order` over `bundled_skill("habeas-refactor")`. `bundled_skill` collapses whitespace, so phrases that span line breaks still match. The helper panics unless each phrase appears after the previous one. I compared the phrases with `assets/skills/habeas-refactor/SKILL.md#section[Habeas refactor]/section[Workflow]`, steps 1–7.

Each obligation maps to an asserted phrase, and the assertions also enforce the order the requirement gives:
- **Move with the agent's own edits, kept separate from other changes.** "Make the move with your own edits" and "Change nothing else in this step" match step 1.
- **Run `habeas refactor --dry-run` with a mapping for every moved file, node and definition name** (cited `requirements.refactor.dry_run` and `requirements.refactor.mappings`). The full phrase "`habeas refactor --dry-run` with one `--map <old>=<new>` for every moved file or directory, node, and definition name" matches step 2. The step-2 sub-bullets for the three mapping forms are not asserted by this test. They illustrate the form of the mappings. They are not separate obligations of the subject.
- **Review the report, including records left unchanged and the rationale spans it lists** (cited `requirements.refactor.rationale.untouched`). Three phrases cover this in step 3: "Review the report", "lists the records it updates, with each code span in their rationales that still mentions an old path", and "lists records a mapping affects that fail a check". The last one is the "Would leave ... unchanged" bullet.
- **Run without `--dry-run`.** "Run the same command without `--dry-run`" matches step 4.
- **Confirm with `habeas status` that only the reported records are stale.** "`habeas status`. Only the records the report left unchanged" matches step 5.
- **Commit the move and evidence update before changing behavior.** The step-6 phrase "Commit the move, the rewritten references, and the `evidence/` changes together, before any change to behavior or text" is asserted.
- **Then reassess stale records with `habeas author` under the habeas-evidence skill.** The step-7 phrase "Next, reassess what remains stale with `habeas author --all`, following the habeas-evidence skill" is asserted.

If the skill dropped, reworded or reordered any of these steps, the test would fail. I found no obligation without an assertion and no plausible requirement-violating skill text that this test would accept. The cited requirements are context only, and I did not reassess their tests or implementations. No `{fixme}` acknowledgments apply.

text: :::{req} refactor_skill.workflow
The `habeas-refactor` skill MUST direct agents to make the move with their own
edits, keeping it separate from any change to the moved code or text; to run
`habeas refactor --dry-run` under {cite}`requirements.refactor.dry_run` with a
mapping for every moved file, node, and definition name under
{cite}`requirements.refactor.mappings`; to review its report, including
records it would leave unchanged and the rationale spans it lists under
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.untouched`; to run it without
`--dry-run`; to confirm with `habeas status` that only the reported records
are stale; and to commit the move and evidence update before changing
behavior, then reassess stale records with `habeas author` under the
habeas-evidence skill.
:::{req} dry_run
With `--dry-run`, `habeas refactor` MUST report every change it would make,
in the same form as {cite}`requirements.refactor.command`, and MUST write
nothing.
:::{req} mappings
Each `--map` MUST have one of these forms:
- a file or directory path, which maps that file, or every file under that
directory, to the same relative path under the new side;
- `<file>#<selector>`, which maps one outline node, and its outline
descendants, to the node at the new file and selector;
- a definition name, which maps that full name, and every full name beginning
with it followed by `.`, to the same suffix under the new name.
A mapping whose old side names a recorded definition, or a prefix of one
followed by `.`, MUST be a definition-name mapping.
:::{req} rationale.untouched
`habeas refactor` MUST NOT change rationale text other than the spans
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.names`,
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.paths`, and
{cite}`requirements.refactor.rationale.addresses` cover. For each changed
record, it MUST list the other code spans in the rationale that contain an old
side of a path or node mapping, so the user can review them.
